findings.current: Coût estimé à 0 $ ; frais finaux non confirmés.
findings.proposed: Coût estimé à 0 $US ; frais finaux non confirmés.
findings.reason: Bare `$` is the only MONEY rendering in the shipped fr corpus (the three other fr values that contain a `$` are JavaScript template/code tokens — `${name}`, `$'{'NAME'}'` — not amounts; counted in audit.log). The corpus writes the currency as the ISO code after the amount (`ui.common.account.low_credits_dialog.detail` « {detail} USD », `ui.providers.phone.action.activate` « Activer pour {amount} USD par mois », `ui.providers.phone.consent` « … à {amount} USD par mois … »), and the runtime's own fr money formatter renders USD as `0,00 $US` (Intl.NumberFormat('fr', {style:'currency', currency:'USD'}).format(0) = "0,00\u00a0$US"). An unqualified `$` is read as CAD in a Canadian reading, while this is a USD billing sentence. Not MAJOR: the amount is zero, so no charge can be misread, and the sentence's real claim (estimate, not a confirmed bill) survives.
findings.current_applicability: Source, target and context key blocks are unchanged from the selected parent; finding remains applicable.

findings.reason: `Son` is correct French and matches the namespace's prose (« Impossible de lire ce son », « Son généré »), but as a standalone label it is homographic with the possessive determiner `son`, and it is always read after a verb: `ui.chat.audio.play_label` is « Lire {label} », so the accessible names become « Lire Son » / « Lire Son 2 ». The namespace's own noun for the media type in a name position is `audio` (« Pièce jointe audio indisponible », « … sera facturée si elle produit un audio »). « Audio » is unambiguous there and costs no width (5 characters, shorter than English's « Sound »).

findings.problem: Bare `$` is the only MONEY rendering in the shipped fr corpus (the three other fr values that contain a `$` are JavaScript template/code tokens — `${name}`, `$'{'NAME'}'` — not amounts; counted in audit.log). findings.replacement: Coût estimé à 0 $US ; frais finaux non confirmés.
findings.replacement_note: U+00A0 between `0` and `$US`, U+202F before `;`. If the integrator prefers the corpus prose form over the symbol, « Coût estimé à 0 USD ; frais finaux non confirmés. » is equally correct and is the more consistent choice with the three shipped USD strings. Either keeps the sentence the sidecar forbids shortening to « Sans frais ».

findings.problem: `Son` is correct French and matches the namespace's prose (« Impossible de lire ce son », « Son généré »), but as a standalone label it is homographic with the possessive determiner `son`, and it is always read after a verb: `ui.chat.audio.play_label` is « Lire {label} », so the accessible names become « Lire Son » / « Lire Son 2 ». findings.replacement_note: Non-gating and a judgement call: a sighted reader is not misled by « Son 2 » in the player, and a screen-reader listener hears it in an audio context. Change only if the integrator wants the accessible-name composition to stand alone; if changed, keep « Son généré » and « ce son » as they are (prose, where the homograph does not arise).
